topic: Exact continuous-outcome canonical gradients for hidden ordered multilevel treatments. Observe iid O=(Y,A,Z,X) with fixed K>=3 latent J, bounded common-support Y, K-category surrogate A and proxy Z, conditional three-view independence, latent ignorability, uniform positivity, separated measurement and outcome-feature factors, modal-label margin, and fixed-rank posterior and Gram operators. For psi_j=E[E(Y|J=j,X)] and every fixed full-rank contrast C with C1=0, prove that the Bian--Zhou--Cui product-bridge influence function becomes canonical after a pointwise K²-cell weighted projection and one conditional Gram solve of dimension at most 2K². Prove tangent-space completeness, strict variance reduction iff the projected correction is nonzero, coherent-nuisance quadratic mean bias and linear L² score stability, and efficient cross-fitted joint Gaussian/max-t inference under explicit product rates. Consumer: an augmented Bodory--Busshoff--Lechner six-bin maternal-smoking/birth-weight study with paired self-report and cotinine proxy. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Coherent factorization makes both linear measurement-error terms vanish against the true score constraints, giving |P khat| bounded by a constant times (r_A+r_Z)||khat-k||₂+r_A r_Z; fixed-rank pseudoinverse stability then supplies the proposed quadratic remainder. On a positive K=3 common-support continuous witness, the projector matches an independently differentiated Fisher solve to 2.49e-14, its Gram rank is 12, and raw-minus-efficient covariance has positive eigenvalues 0.622, 1.214, and 1.589. Coherent joint perturbations show quadratic bias; A-only and outcome-only perturbations are unbiased numerically. Searches exposed and credited categorical bridge prior art but found no exact continuous projector collision. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove that the full observed-data DQM tangent closure equals the closure generated by latent additive factor scores, with measurable conditional-X recovery through a bounded differential inverse of the separated three-view tensor. EARLY KILL TEST: At constant X and arbitrary bounded common-support outcome densities, explicitly invert the observed factor-score map and reproduce the continuous witness and coherent perturbation checks; a missing tangent direction or surviving first-order admissible perturbation invalidates efficiency. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/eid_hidden_ordinal_eif_operator.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Does the Bian–Zhou–Cui product-bridge influence function become the canonical gradient for continuous-outcome contrasts of a fixed-K ordered hidden treatment after projecting its K² cell terms onto the observed three-view tangent closure?

source_refs.claim: Derives an observed-data product-bridge influence function for hidden actions but does not characterize it as the observed-data canonical gradient; the main development is binary.
source_refs.author: Zeyu Bian, Ying Zhou, and Yifan Cui

source_refs.claim: Develops identification and semiparametric estimation for a hidden static treatment using a surrogate and auxiliary proxy, centered on a binary-treatment setup.
source_refs.author: Ying Zhou and Eric J. Tchetgen Tchetgen

source_refs.claim: Describes general semiparametric theory and influence-function estimation for array-decomposition causal effects as an open direction.
source_refs.author: Helen Guo, Elizabeth L. Ogburn, and Ilya Shpitser

source_refs.excerpt: Attempt to define a common tangent space and observable influence function across latent refinements.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The product-bridge literature establishes a valid pathwise-derivative representation but does not characterize the full observed-data nuisance tangent space or prove that the representation is its canonical projection. A prior CausalSmith attempt also found that unrestricted latent refinements defeat construction of a common regular tangent model. Fixing K and imposing separated three-view factors removes that cardinality obstruction only if the differential of the observed tensor-factorization map has a measurable, uniformly bounded inverse on the admissible score range. Algebraic factor recovery and a numerically verified Gram projection do not prove that every observed DQM direction is generated by latent additive scores.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem constructing a measurable bounded differential inverse, proving equality of the observed DQM tangent closure and the image closure of latent additive scores, and deriving the unique canonical gradient via an at-most-2K² conditional Gram solve with strict variance reduction exactly when its projected correction is nonzero.

writing_exemplar.why: Its bridge-versus-array comparison most directly frames why latent-factor identification still lacks a general observed-data efficiency theory.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Proxies identify causal targets despite hidden variables -> array decomposition recovers latent factors under distinct assumptions -> semiparametric theory for array-identified effects remains nascent -> derive the exact canonical gradient for ordered multilevel hidden treatment

method_exemplars.technique: Strengthen three-view tensor uniqueness into local differential inversion, then prove that the inverse is measurable and bounded on the admissible score range.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The required tangent-completeness result is the differential analogue of three-view latent-factor recoverability.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over the product-bridge construction, multiply robust remainder expansion, and asymptotic-linearity argument, then project the resulting gradient onto the smaller static three-view tangent space.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its influence function has the same product-bridge architecture as the candidate whose canonicality and efficient inference must be established.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the observed-data efficient-score projection for a latent covariate measured with error, including its conditional-expectation description of nuisance scores.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the classical measurement-error tangent-projection template needed to justify the finite conditional Gram solve.

open_problems.open_problem: Can confidence regions for the hidden-treatment contrast Cψ remain uniformly valid along local sequences where the smallest measurement-factor or projection-Gram singular value approaches zero?

source_refs.claim: Develops root-n inference for strongly identified linear functionals when conditional-moment nuisance functions are weakly identified or nonunique.
source_refs.author: Andrew Bennett, Nathan Kallus, Xiaojie Mao, Whitney Newey, Vasilis Syrgkanis, and Masatoshi Uehara

source_refs.claim: Treats array-decomposition semiparametric estimation as nascent and relies on qualitative invertibility rather than local-to-singularity inference.
source_refs.author: Helen Guo, Elizabeth L. Ogburn, and Ilya Shpitser

source_refs.claim: Proves asymptotic normality under fixed proxy-relevance conditions rather than inference uniform over vanishing separation.
source_refs.author: Zeyu Bian, Ying Zhou, and Yifan Cui

open_problems.why_unsolved: Fixed-rank arguments rely on stable pseudoinverses and a nonsingular conditional Gram system. When a singular value shrinks, the projected gradient and its variance can diverge, so ordinary cross-fitted Gaussian approximations need not be uniform. Existing weak-proxy theory concerns linear conditional-moment operators; here the weak object is a nonlinear finite-rank three-view factorization followed by a tangent projection. No located result supplies local asymptotic theory for that composition.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A local-asymptotic characterization indexed by the decay rate of the smallest measurement or Gram singular value, including the minimax rate or limiting experiment for Cψ and a confidence set with uniform coverage across regular and weak-separation regimes.

writing_exemplar.why: It clearly separates weak identification of nuisance structure from possible strong identification of the causal functional.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Proxy nuisances can be ill-posed -> fixed-strength assumptions hide nonuniform behavior -> low-dimensional causal functionals may remain estimable -> characterize inference for hidden-treatment contrasts near tensor singularity

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt penalized minimax estimation of primary and debiasing nuisances and its functional strong-identification proof, replacing the linear operator by the differential of the tensor-factor map composed with Cψ.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Cψ is a low-dimensional causal functional of a potentially weakly recovered latent law, matching the paper's central structural distinction.

method_exemplars.technique: Use source-condition regularization and constrained minimax estimation to control strong L² error without a closed-range assumption, after deriving a corresponding source condition for the factor-score differential.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides rate machinery for inverse problems near nonidentification, needed before a uniform Gaussian approximation can be proved.

open_problems.open_problem: Under explicit ε-bounded violations of three-view conditional independence or latent ignorability, what is the sharp sensitivity region and first-order bias map for the ordered multilevel contrast Cψ?

source_refs.claim: Derives bias formulas for violations of proximal assumptions in a linear structural equation model and presents them as a first step toward broader sensitivity analysis.
source_refs.author: Raluca Cobzaru, Roy Welsch, Stan Finkelstein, Kenney Ng, and Zach Shahn

source_refs.claim: Identifies a hidden treatment under exact surrogate and proxy restrictions, leaving departures from those restrictions outside the point-identified model.
source_refs.author: Ying Zhou and Eric J. Tchetgen Tchetgen

source_refs.claim: Provides proxy-based partial identification when completeness fails but not sensitivity regions for failures of conditional independence and latent ignorability in hidden-treatment tensor models.
source_refs.author: AmirEmad Ghassami, Ilya Shpitser, and Eric J. Tchetgen Tchetgen

open_problems.why_unsolved: The identifying law uses exact factorization of the three views given J and X and exact latent ignorability. In the smoking application, self-report and cotinine can share timing, reporting, or metabolic mechanisms that induce residual dependence. Available violation formulas use linear covariance algebra and do not cover multilevel latent treatments, nonlinear tensor recovery, or arbitrary bounded continuous outcome densities. The first broken proof step is the additive factorization of observed scores: an ε-violation introduces cross-view interaction scores that can survive the nominal orthogonality correction.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem giving the Gateaux derivative and worst-case bias of Cψ over an ε-indexed class of conditional-independence and ignorability violations, together with a sharp or demonstrably valid sensitivity interval that collapses to the efficient point-identified estimand at ε=0.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates sensitivity analysis from the untestability of proxy assumptions and the possibility of large, unintuitive violation bias.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Proxy methods replace no-unmeasured-confounding with other untestable restrictions -> violations can create substantial bias -> current formulas are confined to linear models -> quantify sharp sensitivity for nonlinear ordered hidden-treatment recovery

method_exemplars.technique: Generalize its explicit violation-parameter bias decomposition from covariance equations to the Fréchet derivative of the three-view factorization and projected contrast.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems seek a mathematical map from proxy-assumption violations to causal-effect bias.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt smooth approximations and bootstrap confidence intervals for nonsmooth proxy-bound endpoints to the ε-indexed sensitivity extrema.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed sensitivity region is a partially identified causal target whose estimated endpoints inherit the same nonsmooth-inference problem.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the sharp identified set for Cψ when a hidden-treatment measurement factor loses rank or the modal-label margin is weakened to non-strict ordinal information?

source_refs.claim: Shows that proxies can yield causal-effect bounds without completeness, but studies proximal hidden-confounder and hidden-mediator settings rather than tensor-recovered ordered hidden treatment.
source_refs.author: AmirEmad Ghassami, Ilya Shpitser, and Eric J. Tchetgen Tchetgen

source_refs.claim: Explains that array decomposition identifies latent factors only up to labels and that strict central-tendency ordering is one way to recover hidden-treatment labels.
source_refs.author: Helen Guo, Elizabeth L. Ogburn, and Ilya Shpitser

source_refs.claim: Provides generic three-view latent-class identifiability under Kruskal rank conditions, leaving rank-deficient points outside its point-identification guarantee.
source_refs.author: Elizabeth S. Allman, Catherine Matias, and John A. Rhodes

open_problems.why_unsolved: Tensor results provide generic point identification up to permutation under rank conditions, while hidden-treatment analyses resolve permutations through strict surrogate informativeness or ordering. Existing proxy partial-identification work does not characterize feasible latent decompositions, weakly ordered labelings, and continuous outcome-feature factors in this model. Rank loss makes the inverse factor map set-valued, and a weak order only partially eliminates permutations, so Cψ must be optimized jointly over observationally equivalent factorizations rather than evaluated through a single bridge.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp finite- or infinite-dimensional optimization characterization of the identified set for Cψ over all bounded continuous-outcome three-view factorizations matching the observed law, with necessary and sufficient conditions for the set to collapse to a singleton.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames failure of an untestable proxy completeness condition as a reason to replace point identification with informative bounds.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Proxy point identification uses strong relevance conditions -> those conditions can fail and are difficult to verify -> proxies may still constrain the causal target -> derive sharp bounds under tensor-rank or label-margin failure

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt sum-of-ratios fractional programming for proxy partial identification, replacing its hidden-confounder feasible set with tensor-factorization, stochastic-matrix, order, and bounded-outcome constraints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems optimize a causal functional over proxy-compatible latent laws when point-identifying operator conditions fail.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over smooth approximation and bootstrap inference for nonsmooth bound endpoints, adding control of estimated tensor-feasibility constraints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies an inference route for proxy-derived bound endpoints once the latent-factor identified set is characterized.

open_problems.open_problem: When three-view tensor factors are recovered only pointwise in X, what conditions guarantee a unique globally measurable ordinal labeling of the K hidden treatment states when proxy-location curves can touch or cross?

source_refs.claim: Identifies three-view latent-class parameters generically only up to latent-state permutation.
source_refs.author: Elizabeth S. Allman, Catherine Matias, and John A. Rhodes

source_refs.claim: Uses a location restriction to index eigenfunctions uniquely but does not address X-dependent discrete label crossings in an ordered hidden-treatment model.
source_refs.author: Yingyao Hu and Susanne M. Schennach

source_refs.claim: States that label recovery is essential for hidden-treatment counterfactuals and lists strict ordering restrictions without a measurable conditional-X alignment theorem at crossings.
source_refs.author: Helen Guo, Elizabeth L. Ogburn, and Ilya Shpitser

open_problems.why_unsolved: Kruskal and eigendecomposition arguments recover only an unordered set of latent factors at each covariate value. A strict modal or monotone margin chooses a local permutation, but when location curves meet or exchange order, independently selected pointwise permutations need not form a measurable, causally coherent global labeling. Existing indexing restrictions settle labels in different measurement-error models but do not characterize the permutation bundle induced by conditional-X tensor recovery.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A measurable-selection and identification theorem giving necessary and sufficient conditions for the pointwise permutation bundle to admit a unique ordinal section across X, plus a counterexample establishing nonidentification of Cψ when those conditions fail.

writing_exemplar.why: It directly explains why factor recovery up to labels is insufficient for hidden-treatment counterfactuals and organizes existing label-recovery assumptions.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Array decomposition recovers latent factors only up to permutation -> causal treatment levels require meaningful labels -> strict pointwise ordering resolves labels locally -> determine when local labels glue into a measurable global ordinal treatment

method_exemplars.technique: Start from Kruskal uniqueness modulo the finite permutation group and analyze the resulting X-indexed orbit map, constructing a measurable global section instead of choosing a permutation at one fixed law.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the exact pointwise identification object whose residual permutation ambiguity must be resolved.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt eigenfunction indexing by a location functional, replacing one global normalization with covariate-indexed ordinal inequalities and continuity or separation conditions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its proof shows how substantively meaningful location restrictions remove decomposition-label ambiguity.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over joint-diagonalization estimation and asymptotic theory for repeated-measurement mixtures, adding a label-alignment step stable away from crossing sets.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It estimates the same type of repeated-measurement latent factors and provides the nearest inferential machinery once coherent labels are identified.

literature_map:
Zhou and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2024, arXiv:2405.09080) is the closest static anchor: it recovers a hidden treatment from a surrogate and proxy, but its indexed core model is binary.
Bian, Zhou, and Cui (2026, arXiv:2607.25241) derive a product-bridge influence function for hidden actions; observed-data canonical efficiency is not established.
Guo, Ogburn, and Shpitser (2025, arXiv:2512.00175) contrast bridge equations with array decomposition and identify general semiparametric theory for array-identified causal effects as future work.
Allman, Matias, and Rhodes (2009, Annals of Statistics, doi:10.1214/09-AOS689) provide foundational generic identification for three-view latent structures, up to labels.
Hu and Schennach (2008, Econometrica, doi:10.1111/j.0012-9682.2008.00823.x) use operator decomposition and a location normalization for nonclassical measurement error.
Bonhomme, Jochmans, and Robin (2016, JRSSB, doi:10.1111/rssb.12110) give constructive repeated-measurement mixture recovery, joint-diagonalization estimation, and asymptotic inference.
Cui, Pu, Shi, Miao, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2024, JASA, doi:10.1080/01621459.2023.2191817) derive efficient influence functions for proximal hidden-confounder bridges, not hidden multilevel treatments.
Ghassami, Ying, Shpitser, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2022, AISTATS, arXiv:2104.02929) develop minimax kernel learning and asymptotic linearity for doubly robust integral-equation functionals.
Kallus, Mao, and Uehara (2021, arXiv:2103.14029) separate identification of causal functionals from uniqueness of negative-control bridge functions.
Zhang, Li, Miao, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2023, Statistics & Probability Letters, doi:10.1016/j.spl.2023.109836) study proximal identification and root-n estimation without unique bridges.
Bennett et al. (2023, COLT/PMLR 195) develop normal inference for strongly identified linear functionals of weakly identified inverse-problem nuisances.
Ghassami, Shpitser, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2023, arXiv:2304.04374) and Zhang–Su (2024, UAI/PMLR 244) provide proxy partial-identification methods when point identification fails.
Cobzaru et al. (2024, Journal of Causal Inference, doi:10.1515/jci-2023-0039) derive proximal-assumption violation bias formulas only for linear structural equations.
Bodory, Busshoff, and Lechner (2022, Entropy, doi:10.3390/e24081039) and Zimmert–Lechner (2019, arXiv:1908.08779) frame the maternal-smoking application but assume observed treatment.
No located paper combines K≥3 ordered hidden treatment, arbitrary bounded continuous outcomes, paired categorical views, an explicit K²-cell canonical projection, tangent-space completeness, and efficient joint contrast inference.
